specPoints.text: describe a DNA molecule as two strands coiled to form a double helix, the strands being linked by a series of paired bases: adenine (A) with thymine (T), and cytosine (C) with guanine (G)

primer.text: Before you can talk mutations or protein synthesis you need the shape of the molecule itself. This note assembles DNA from its parts — two strands, a sugar-phosphate backbone, four bases — and locks in the pairing rule, adenine with thymine and cytosine with guanine, that makes the double helix copyable as a template.

lessons.title: The Double Helix and Its Pairing Rule
lessons.opening: DNA is the cell's genetic material, a two-stranded polymer wound into a double helix, whose sugar-phosphate backbones are bridged by paired bases obeying one rule: adenine always faces thymine, and cytosine always faces guanine.
keyPoints: DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid and sits in the nucleus.
Two strands coil around each other to form the double helix.
Each strand is a sugar-phosphate backbone carrying the bases A, T, G and C.
Complementary pairing links A with T and G with C.
Each half helix acts as a template when copying is needed.

low.restatement: DNA is a two-stranded molecule whose bases click together in fixed couples.
low.analogy: A spiral ladder where each rung is a matching pair: only certain rungs fit.
low.examPointer: Use full base names in written answers, not just the letters.

medium.restatement: The pairing rule is what makes the helix a copying machine: either strand determines its partner exactly.
medium.analogy: A zip whose teeth only close in one combination, so one half predicts the other.
medium.examPointer: Link the template idea to both cell division and protein synthesis.

check.stem: What shape do the two strands of DNA coil into?

options.text: Two strands coiled into a double helix
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
That describes RNA, not DNA.
No such DNA form exists in the taught account.
The strands coil, they do not lie flat.

check.stem: Which bases are paired as complements?

options.text: A with T, and C with G
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: A with G, and T with C
options.explanation: The purines do not pair with each other.

options.text: A with C, and T with G
options.explanation: That pairing breaks the taught rule.
Pairing is fixed, not random.

check.stem: What forms the backbone of each DNA strand?

options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Those build proteins, not DNA.
Fats play no part in the DNA backbone.
The bases project from the backbone; they are not the backbone.

check.stem: Name the four bases found in DNA.

options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Uracil belongs to RNA, not DNA.

check.stem: Why do cell division and protein synthesis depend on the pairing rules?

options.text: Each strand serves as a template that the rules let you copy exactly
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: Pairing stores energy for the cell
options.explanation: Energy storage is not the pairing rule's role.

options.text: The rules speed up the nucleus
options.explanation: The nucleus does not accelerate through pairing.

options.text: The helix glows when correctly paired
options.explanation: Nothing glows; the value is fidelity of copying.

check.stem: State the complementary partner of each DNA base.
check.modelAnswer: Adenine pairs with thymine, and cytosine pairs with guanine.

check.stem: Describe a DNA molecule using the words polymer, strands and helix.
check.modelAnswer: DNA is a polymer of two strands coiled together as a double helix.

check.stem: Explain why the word template is used for each half of the double helix.
check.modelAnswer: Because bases pair in a fixed way, an existing strand determines exactly which bases join its partner, so each half guides the rebuilding of a complete identical helix.

check.stem: One DNA strand reads A-T-G-C along a region. Write the sequence its partner strand must carry in that region.
check.modelAnswer: The partner must read T-A-C-G, since A faces T and C faces G in complementary pairing.

glossary.definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid, the genetic material held in the nucleus.
The two-stranded coil formed by the DNA molecule.
The fixed rule that adenine pairs with thymine and cytosine pairs with guanine.
A strand whose bases dictate exactly which bases join to rebuild its partner.
